rules.requirement: Record and set mutations SHOULD capture actor, target, selection or identity, time, outcome, and correlation identifier.
Measures MUST declare their output grain; combining different grains without an explicit reaggregation is invalid.
Aggregate functions MUST support the input type and define empty-input behavior.
Operations that require full materialization (for example global sort) MUST NOT run on an unbounded stream without a window or other bound.
Deduplication MUST define identity key and deterministic survivor selection.
Distinct/intersect/except/deduplicate MUST define or infer equality/key semantics compatible with the item type.
Referenced fields MUST exist at the current pipeline stage, not merely in the original source.
Filter predicates MUST evaluate to boolean.
Group keys MUST be hashable/comparable under the execution profile and output grouping keys MUST be retained or deliberately discarded.
Every collection operation MUST receive a known item schema or type.
Many-to-many or otherwise fanout-producing joins SHOULD require an explicit expected-cardinality declaration.
Both join inputs and join fields MUST resolve.
Join key types, units, null semantics, and cardinalities MUST be compatible.
`map` MUST preserve item count; `flat-map` MUST declare zero-to-many output cardinality.
A required deterministic sort MUST provide a total order or stable tie-breaker.
The validator MUST derive or verify the output schema after each operation.
Partition keys MUST exist and partitioning MUST preserve required grouping/order guarantees.
Projected output field names MUST be unique.
A collection transformation SHOULD be pure. Any external state mutation MUST be declared as a command/effect boundary.
Sampling MUST define method, valid size/rate, seed or nondeterminism policy, and stratification keys where applicable.
Union/intersect/except inputs MUST have compatible schemas and equality semantics.
Windows MUST define type, size/gap, ordering/time field, time zone, lateness/watermark policy for streams, and emission policy.
Multi-step, nontransactional commands SHOULD define compensation or reconciliation behavior.
Sequential dependencies MUST be ordered; independent actions MAY run concurrently only when their read/write sets do not conflict.
Saga-like flows MUST define forward actions, compensations, durable state, retry policy, and terminal failure behavior.
Read-modify-write actions MUST prevent or explicitly accept lost updates.
Optimistic concurrency MUST identify a version or comparison token and define conflict behavior.

Every action-like construct MUST declare or unambiguously resolve all fields required to validate its effect, operation, scope, target, input/output shape, authorization, failure behavior, and applicable transaction semantics.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Destructive actions MUST require a specific permission; generic read/write permission is insufficient under a strict profile.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Human-facing destructive bulk actions SHOULD require confirmation proportional to impact.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Delete, bulk-delete, destructive replace, command, firmware, and control actions MUST be explicitly classified as destructive where applicable.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Recovery, rollback, backup, or irreversibility MUST be declared for material destructive actions.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Deletion MUST respect retention, legal hold, audit, security, and archival rules.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Destructive set actions MUST expose the evaluated target count or preview when technically feasible.

rules.section: Safety and authorization for destructive actions
rules.requirement: Device commands and control actions MUST validate target capability, current state, interlocks, permissives, range, units, acknowledgment, timeout, and fail-safe behavior.
Events describing state changes MUST be emitted only if the corresponding change commits, using an outbox/equivalent guarantee when required.
Event consumers MUST declare duplicate-handling when delivery can be at least once.
Event payloads MUST reflect the declared before/after semantics and MUST obey classification/minimization policies.
Conditionally idempotent actions MUST state the condition/key that makes repetition safe.
Retriable create/bulk-create/upsert operations MUST use a stable idempotency or identity key.
Delete SHOULD be idempotent under its not-found policy.
The caller's actor/role/system MUST be authorized for the action, target, scope, and selection.
A query-only context MUST NOT invoke a command. A pure transform MUST NOT invoke an undeclared stateful effect.
Callers MUST handle or propagate declared failure modes.
Supplied arguments MUST cover required inputs exactly once and match names, types, cardinalities, units, and classifications.
Consumers MUST handle the declared output shape, including optional, many, stream, and per-item failure results.
The caller MUST establish or explicitly handle action preconditions.
Recursive action invocation MUST be explicitly allowed and have a bounded/terminating strategy.
Every invoked action MUST resolve to one canonical action contract.
A record-oriented caller MUST NOT invoke a set mutation accidentally through an ambiguous reference.
Remote/long-running actions SHOULD define timeout and cancellation behavior.
Nested action transaction requirements MUST be compatible; impossible propagation combinations MUST be errors.
`create` MUST provide every required, noncomputed field not supplied by a default or generation policy.
`create` MUST return or emit the created identity unless the execution profile explicitly defines asynchronous identity delivery.
`create` MUST NOT accept client assignments to computed, generated, or unauthorized read-only fields.
`delete` MUST identify hard-delete, soft-delete, archive, or tombstone behavior and MUST respect relation/retention policies.
`exists` MUST return boolean and MUST NOT expose record data as a side effect.
`read`, `replace`, `update`, `patch`, and `delete` MUST provide a selection that is provably unique. A non-unique predicate makes the operation set-scoped.
Read/mutation operations MUST define not-found behavior: empty result, domain error, or idempotent success where appropriate.
`patch` MUST declare its patch dialect and MUST validate every path, operation, and value type.
Mutations MUST establish declared field, relation, lifecycle, and invariant postconditions.
Version, state, ownership, and business preconditions MUST be checked before mutation.
`replace` MUST supply every required mutable field. Omitted optional fields MUST follow an explicit clear/preserve policy.
A record CRUD action MUST target exactly one entity or record-shaped resource.
`update` MUST declare which fields may change and MUST NOT mutate fields outside that set.
`upsert` MUST identify a stable conflict key and MUST define behavior when more than one existing record matches.
Retries MUST be bounded and use a valid backoff policy.
Retry policies MUST distinguish transient from permanent failures.
Retrying a non-idempotent command without duplicate suppression or compensation MUST be an error.
A set mutation MUST declare `atomic`, `per-record`, or `best-effort` atomicity.
Bulk upsert MUST define duplicate input-key behavior and conflicts among concurrently processed items.
Bulk delete/update cascades MUST be bounded, authorized, and consistent with the consuming stack's declared relation ownership.
Bulk mutations MUST define conflict handling when records can change between selection and mutation.
A set operation MUST declare `scope = "set"` or another collection scope. It MUST NOT masquerade as record CRUD.
Bulk input records MUST have a uniform compatible schema unless the operation explicitly supports tagged variants.
Entity and cross-record invariants MUST hold at the declared atomicity boundary.
Limits MUST be positive; limits without deterministic order SHOULD produce a warning.
An operation whose result/effect depends on order MUST declare a stable ordering and tie-breaker.
Results MUST declare whether they return affected records, keys, count, per-item outcomes, or no value.
Large/unbounded queries MUST declare or inherit pagination, streaming, or bounded materialization behavior.
Nonatomic operations MUST expose per-item success and failure results and MUST define retry behavior.
`query` and `count` MUST have `effect = "query"` and MUST NOT mutate modeled state.
Bulk update/patch/delete MUST specify a selection. Absence of a selection MUST be an error; selecting every record requires an explicit `all` selection.
Synchronization MUST declare source of truth, identity matching, create/update/delete behavior, and conflict precedence.
An unbounded or `all` mutation SHOULD produce a high-severity warning and MAY require explicit approval.
A transaction MUST NOT claim atomicity across systems that cannot provide it; use compensation/outbox/reconciliation semantics instead.
Multi-record invariants requiring atomicity MUST execute in a compatible transaction boundary.
Security/privacy classification MUST propagate unless a validated declassification, masking, anonymization, or aggregation rule applies.
Deterministic transformations MUST not depend on undeclared time, randomness, environment, or mutable external state.
Every output field MUST trace to source fields, constants, generated values, or an explicitly opaque computation.
Transformations used for synchronization/upsert MUST preserve or explicitly remap identity.
Narrowing, truncating, rounding, dropping, lossy encoding, or many-to-one conversion MUST be declared and SHOULD warn.
Null/missing/error behavior MUST be declared for each transformation that can fail or lose presence information.
Nondeterministic transformations SHOULD record seeds, versions, parameters, and execution context when reproducibility matters.
Every required target field MUST be mapped, defaulted, generated, or computed.
If a transformation claims reversibility, round-trip validation MUST show that required information is preserved.
Persistence, messaging, command dispatch, and external calls MUST be modeled separately from the pure transformation or explicitly declared as effects.
Source and target schemas/types MUST resolve.
Time conversions MUST preserve instant/local-time semantics and explicitly handle time zones and daylight-saving ambiguity.
A transformation MUST declare whether it is total or how unsupported/invalid inputs are handled.
Field transformations MUST produce values compatible with target types, constraints, units, and cardinality.
Unit changes MUST use an explicit valid conversion.
Transformation/schema versions MUST be compatible; migrations MUST define supported source and destination versions.
Security-sensitive, approval, policy, and automated actions SHOULD identify an audit or evidence path.
Governed production constructs SHOULD identify an accountable owner.
Cycles MUST be rejected in graphs declared acyclic. Cycles in executable graphs MUST have an explicit exit or termination condition.
A nonterminal executable node without an outgoing path SHOULD produce a warning or error according to the graph kind.
Duplicate equivalent edges SHOULD be rejected or warned unless parallel edges are meaningful and explicitly distinguished.
Every edge endpoint MUST resolve to a node in the graph or to an explicitly permitted external endpoint.
Self-edges MUST be rejected unless the construct explicitly supports them.
Required terminal nodes MUST be reachable from a valid entry node.
Unreachable nodes SHOULD produce warnings.
The module import graph MUST be acyclic, except for an explicitly documented type-only cycle supported by the resolver.
Import aliases MUST be unique in a model.
Every external grammar reference MUST use a declared import.
Every imported module and production MUST exist.
Every model module MUST be declared in `grammar-stack.json`.
A reference MUST resolve to the construct kind required by its position. For example, a role reference cannot resolve to an entity.
A qualified name MUST resolve to exactly one accessible declaration.
Reserved keywords MUST NOT be used as identifiers.
Shadowing an imported or enclosing declaration SHOULD produce a warning unless explicitly annotated as intentional.
Names MUST be unique among declarations of conflicting kinds in the same lexical scope.
Unreferenced private declarations SHOULD produce a warning.
A reference MUST NOT access a declaration outside its permitted or exported scope.
Executable integrations, pipelines, and deployments SHOULD define failure reporting and operational observability.
Stage indexes SHOULD be contiguous unless sparse ordering is explicitly supported.
Explicit indexes, priorities, sequence numbers, and ordering keys MUST be unique within their containing scope.
A grammar MUST reference, rather than redefine, a construct owned by another grammar. Each consuming stack MUST publish its concrete ownership map and validate every cross-module boundary against it.
A construct with a single-owner relationship MUST have exactly one owner.
Source, target, input, output, from, and to references MUST point in the direction required by the construct.
Removing or deprecating a declaration MUST NOT leave dangling references.
Every reference MUST resolve to exactly one declaration.
A machine-readable model or manifest MUST conform to its declared versioned schema before deeper semantic validation.
An executable action MUST have an applicable authorization rule or an explicit public/system exemption.
Data or control crossing a trust boundary MUST have an applicable security control.
Granted permissions SHOULD be no broader than required by referenced actions.
Secrets and credentials MUST NOT appear as literal scalar values; they MUST be references to protected secret material.
The configured start production MUST exist.
Durations, intervals, timeouts, backoffs, retention periods, and windows MUST be nonnegative; execution intervals and timeouts that must advance time MUST be greater than zero.
Schedule expressions MUST parse according to the configured schedule dialect and MUST identify a time zone when interpretation would otherwise be ambiguous.
Windows, sampling frequencies, retention, and aggregation intervals MUST be mutually compatible.
Type aliases MUST NOT form a cycle.
Assigned and default values MUST be compatible with the destination type.
Collection element types and cardinalities MUST be compatible in assignments, mappings, and bindings.
Conditions, guards, filters, and transition predicates MUST evaluate to boolean.
An enum value MUST belong to its declared enum.
Every declared type MUST resolve to a primitive, alias, enum, schema, entity, or other valid type declaration.
A required value MUST NOT receive a null or missing value. Optionality and cardinality MUST be preserved through mappings.
Operators MUST accept the operand types supplied and MUST produce the type expected by the surrounding expression.
Defaults MUST satisfy the same validation rules as runtime values.
Numeric values used for execution, thresholds, weights, or probabilities MUST be finite.
Numeric values MUST satisfy applicable minimum, maximum, positivity, percentage, probability, capacity, duration, and count ranges.
Compared, added, assigned, or mapped quantities MUST use compatible units. Conversions MUST be explicit when units differ.
Referenced module and construct versions MUST satisfy the importing model's supported version range.
Use of a deprecated construct SHOULD produce a warning and identify its replacement.
